newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGB futures end higher, shrug off Fed tightening.
newsitem.headline: JGB futures end higher, shrug off Fed tightening.

text.p: Key June Japanese government bond (JGB) futures ended Wednesday's Tokyo session sharply higher, shrugging off the overnight 25 basis point rate rise by the U.S. Federal Reserve.
The June closed up 0.62 at an intraday high of 125.94. Turnover was 58,819.

Short-covering pressure intensified near the close after the benchmark contract breached the key chart point of 125.75, which represents a half-way retracement from the recent low of 124.63 set on March 24 to the record high of 126.88 set on March 17, traders said.
"The rally was triggered by squaring of short positions set up for hedging before Tuesday's FOMC meeting," said a brokerage house trader.
The Fed's rate hike had little impact on the JGB market as it had been widely expected, traders said.
"The Fed's tightening helped to remove one of the key uncertainties," said a trader at a city bank's securities unit.
Traders said a jump in Euroyen futures also contributed to improving the JGB market's mood.
Key December three-month Euroyen futures ended Wednesday's TIFFE day session at 99.06, up 0.10 from Tuesday.
Investors were detected buying cash JGBs, particularly at the intermediate part of the yield curve, traders said.
The yield of the benchmark cash 182nd JGB stood at 2.275 percent, down from 2.335 percent on Tuesday.
"Short-covering pressure was quite strong in the intermediate sector, which had been weak recently. Large-lot buy orders were seen from investors," said a trader at another brokerage house.
Traders said the new 194th 10-year JGBs auctioned on Tuesday have met with good investor demand, allowing dealers to cover their short positions set up for hedging purposes.

Traders said June JGB futures could test 126.00 in the near future, but a further substantial rise was unlikely before the release of the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) key "tankan" corporate survey on April 2.
"The June is likely to consolidate near 126.00 ahead of the tankan," said the first brokerage house trader.
The BOJ's continuation of accommodative stance in its daily money market operations for the second day on Wednesday provided a boost for JGBs in the morning, traders said.
The BOJ refrained from conducting its regular operation at 9:20 a.m. (0020 GMT) on Wednesday.
